Wall time drifts about ±1.5% between sessions for identical code (E049: 5.19–5.22 s; E059's E046 rebuild ran at 5.19 against an original 5.08). So a time difference under about 0.07 s cannot be resolved in one run.
2. Time is driven by host and launch overhead per step more than by FLOPs. E061 saved about 12 ms per removed 20 px step, roughly twice the conv compute. E062 saved 0.28 s by dropping 3 reduce-overhead Muon graphs per step. E056's ReLU saved 4.8%, more than its byte saving, which points to erf/exp compute in fp32 GELU, not only bytes. My time misses (E056, E059, E061, E062) all came from underestimating per-step and per-call costs. Lesson: removing steps or calls beats removing pixels. The math-identical levers left are merging the Muon calls (≈0.05–0.1 s once NS compute is netted out) and tanh-GELU (plausibly 1–2%).
3. Muon is load-bearing (E062: −3 pp). The renormalized filters (p *= sqrt(out)/||p||) make Muon's lr an angular step size. Muon has no weight decay at all in the code, so filter wd is inert by construction. Lr ×1.5 is probably a small positive (E014 +0.09 at 3 seeds). Higher momentum, at a fixed NS-normalized step magnitude, only changes direction smoothing. In a 225-step run with Lookahead resets I expect neutral to slightly negative.
4. Accuracy is carried by optimizer steps on layers that are still learning. Early resolution drops are cheap. Freezes are cheap only after a layer's learning ends: whitening at 6%, stem at 75%, group 2 at about 90%. Earlier freezes cost (E037, E053, E054, E055). The anneal-to-0 is part of why E028 was free, but moving only the anneal end changes very little.
5. A mechanism nobody has named: the "absolute-step" bookkeeping is not what the descriptions say. whiten_bias_steps = int(0.06 × planned_steps) is compared against the trimmed step index, so after a trim the whitening detach moves later in data progress. Freeze points subtract the trim, while the LR triangle peak (0.23 × total) moves. E063's crash at a 24-step trim suggests the indexing/epoch logic is fragile: the resolution list is indexed per epoch from the trimmed start, and some 20 px or variant combination was likely never warmed, which tripped error_on_recompile. Further trims need a bookkeeping audit.
6. Architecture cuts and activation swaps that change the function (ReLU, stride-2 stem, width cuts) trade at or worse than the dial (about 0.77 s/pp).
7. The recipe probably under-fits: LS 0.3, 9.5 epochs and 100 classes, so I expect clean train top-1 well below 97%. Regularizer additions will not pay.
8. The PCIe judge's times will be 5–10% higher, more if its host is slower, because of item 2.

W5 (contrarian), after E062/E063. The tip is E061: 5.024 s / 0.7534, 225 steps, with seeds 0–2 sitting on the bar.
1. Noise: per-seed SD is about 0.25 pp and the 3-seed SD about 0.15 pp. The rebuild SD is about 0. A recipe whose population mean is about 0.7535 passes seeds 0–2 about half the time. Wall time drifts about ±1.5% between sessions for identical code (E049: 5.19–5.22 s; E059's E046 rebuild ran at 5.19 against an original 5.08). So a time difference under about 0.07 s cannot be resolved in one run.
2. Time is driven by host and launch overhead per step more than by FLOPs. E061 saved about 12 ms per removed 20 px step, roughly twice the conv compute. E062 saved 0.28 s by dropping 3 reduce-overhead Muon graphs per step. E056's ReLU saved 4.8%, more than its byte saving, which points to erf/exp compute in fp32 GELU, not only bytes. My time misses (E056, E059, E061, E062) all came from underestimating per-step and per-call costs. Lesson: removing steps or calls beats removing pixels. The math-identical levers left are merging the Muon calls (≈0.05–0.1 s once NS compute is netted out) and tanh-GELU (plausibly 1–2%).
3. Muon is load-bearing (E062: −3 pp). The renormalized filters (p *= sqrt(out)/||p||) make Muon's lr an angular step size. Muon has no weight decay at all in the code, so filter wd is inert by construction. Lr ×1.5 is probably a small positive (E014 +0.09 at 3 seeds). Higher momentum, at a fixed NS-normalized step magnitude, only changes direction smoothing. In a 225-step run with Lookahead resets I expect neutral to slightly negative.
4. Accuracy is carried by optimizer steps on layers that are still learning. Early resolution drops are cheap. Freezes are cheap only after a layer's learning ends: whitening at 6%, stem at 75%, group 2 at about 90%. Earlier freezes cost (E037, E053, E054, E055). The anneal-to-0 is part of why E028 was free, but moving only the anneal end changes very little.
5. A mechanism nobody has named: the "absolute-step" bookkeeping is not what the descriptions say. whiten_bias_steps = int(0.06 × planned_steps) is compared against the trimmed step index, so after a trim the whitening detach moves later in data progress. Freeze points subtract the trim, while the LR triangle peak (0.23 × total) moves. E063's crash at a 24-step trim suggests the indexing/epoch logic is fragile: the resolution list is indexed per epoch from the trimmed start, and some 20 px or variant combination was likely never warmed, which tripped error_on_recompile. Further trims need a bookkeeping audit.
6. Architecture cuts and activation swaps that change the function (ReLU, stride-2 stem, width cuts) trade at or worse than the dial (about 0.77 s/pp).
7. The recipe probably under-fits: LS 0.3, 9.5 epochs and 100 classes, so I expect clean train top-1 well below 97%. Regularizer additions will not pay.
8. The PCIe judge's times will be 5–10% higher, more if its host is slower, because of item 2.
Unsure about: whether tanh-GELU's saving reaches 1.5%; the cause of E063's crash; the early-trim dose slope past 12 steps.

forecasts.reason: ReLU's outsized saving points to erf/exp compute, so tanh-GELU likely projects ≥1.5% at near-identical accuracy; this is the contrarian call.
Moving only the anneal end changes very little; the effect sits inside rebuild/seed noise.
The 75% freeze is past group 1's learning; expect +≤0.05 pp, below the 0.12 pp threshold.
With renormalized filters, lr sets the angular step; a small gain (~+0.05 pp) is likely but probably under 0.12 pp.
Three cudagraph Muon calls plus Python lr fills per step are real overhead; ~0.05–0.08 s is recoverable after netting out NS compute.
Direction-only smoothing with Lookahead resets in 225 steps; more lag likely hurts slightly.
Diagnostic rerun of the tip; with LS 0.3 and 9 epochs on 100 classes, clean train top-1 is likely ≤90%.

cruxes: Why did E063 crash? Is it an unwarmed shape/variant from the trimmed-index bookkeeping (whitening detach compared against the trimmed step, per-epoch resolution slicing), and does that bookkeeping also mean E061's 'absolute' whitening detach actually moved later?
Is GELU's fused cost partly fp32 erf/exp compute (tanh-GELU saves ≥1.5%) or purely bytes (≈0 saving)?
How much of the per-step time is host/launch overhead (Muon's 3 graph calls, the Python lr loop over 9 groups) versus GPU compute? One CUDA-event versus wall-time trace per phase would settle it.
